title: SHAP explainer logging fails on sklearn types skops rejects; nested model must use cloudpickle
answers: SHAP explainer logging fails with untrusted type sklearn.tree._tree.Tree
mlflow.shap.log_explainer breaks for tree models after skops 0.15
Why does logging a SHAP explainer require skops trusted types?
Save SHAP explainer with sklearn decision tree without extra trust config
body:
Symptom: Logging a SHAP explainer backed by a scikit-learn tree model fails with an untrusted-type error unless the caller supplies extra trust configuration.
Root cause: mlflow/shap/__init__.py:save_explainer called mlflow.sklearn.save_model on the nested model with default serialization (skops), and skops 0.15 rejects sklearn.tree._tree.Tree by default.
Fix pattern: Pass serialization_format=mlflow.sklearn.SERIALIZATION_FORMAT_CLOUDPICKLE for the nested model inside save_explainer. The explainer state is already pickle, so the nested model stays on the same trust boundary. Do not auto-add skops_trusted_types.
Constraints: Applies only to the SHAP-nested sklearn model. Direct mlflow.sklearn.save_model/log_model calls keep the skops default. Tests should expect serialization_format cloudpickle, a model.pkl file, and skops_trusted_types None; pip requirement expectations use mlflow.sklearn.get_default_pip_requirements(include_cloudpickle=True).
applies: Changes to how mlflow/shap serializes its nested scikit-learn or pytorch model; not standalone sklearn serialization.
says: Saving a decision tree model explainer fails with an untrusted type error during experiment tracking.
Allow logging tree model explanations without forcing users to configure custom trusted types.
Tree-based model explainer runs crash because the underlying tree structure is flagged as untrusted.
Model explainers created for decision trees should save successfully out of the box.
Logging an explainer for a trained tree classifier prompts for unnecessary security configurations.
search: Logging a SHAP explainer backed by a scikit-learn tree model fails with an untrusted-type error because `save_explainer` in `mlflow/shap/__init__.py` defaulted to skops, which rejects `sklearn.tree._tree.Tree` in skops 0.15. To fix this, `save_explainer` must serialize nested models using `serialization_format=mlflow.sklearn.SERIALIZATION_FORMAT_CLOUDPICKLE` without auto-adding `skops_trusted_types`. This applies only to SHAP-nested scikit-learn models; standalone `mlflow.sklearn.save_model` and `log_model` calls keep the default skops serialization. Tests in `tests/shap/test_log.py` should assert cloudpickle serialization, a `model.pkl` artifact, `skops_trusted_types` set to None, and pip requirements using `include_cloudpickle=True`.
